newsitem.title: USA: INSIGHT - Dlr lacks stamina, mark/yen may be key.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Dlr lacks stamina, mark/yen may be key.

text.p: The dollar is clearly lacking stamina after its recent selloff and its near-term trend may depend on the mark/yen cross, analysts said on Tuesday.

"On the daily charts, there is a big upside gap on mark/yen between 70.75 and 71.30. One of the big questions is whether we'll be able to fill that gap," said Chris Turner, senior analyst at the consulting firm I.D.E.A.
Turner predicted that failure to fill the gap would lead to a consolidation between 69.70 and 69.30, "quite bearish for mark/yen."
"This would have pretty bearish implications for dollar/yen, suggesting it's just the beginning of the story," Turner also said.
The dollar's setback started late last week on remarks by Japanese officials seen as indicating the U.S. currency would not be allowed to rise further against the yen.
Dollar/yen ended on Tuesday in New York at 118.55/65 -- or almost seven yen off its high on Thursday at 125.35.
"A move below 117.50 yen would be a nasty one, it would be a break to the downside," said Turner who saw range-trading in store for dollar/yen in the 117.50/120.00 area.
Analysts at MCM CurrencyWatch saw very strong support on dollar/yen at 117.60, a 7-1/2-month bull channel. If that support holds, dollar/yen may try to attack 119.70.
On dollar/mark, MCM CurrencyWatch saw strong support at 1.6890 and then 1.6830, with buying opportunities at 1.69 for an upward move likely to top out at 1.7095.
I.D.E.A.'s Turner saw dollar/mark medium-term trading range between 1.7380, the recent high, and 1.6680, the recent low, with 1.6850 and 1.71 as near-term support and resistance.
Dollar/Swiss is moving in tandem with dollar/mark and will not signal a rally unless it takes out the 1.44 level.
"Dollar/mark is moving sideways and dollar/yen should lead the dollar lower," Turner predicted if the near-term ranges do not hold.
